Use a logging package with log_call()

Source: R/log_extend.R
extending_log.Rd

log_call() writes through a logger, see logger_base. To log with another package, inherit from logger_base and register a method for logger_fn(). The package then owns the thresholds, layouts and appenders.

Details

level is the label from the logger's property for the event's level, so "INFO" for an info event. Override the defaults of the trace, debug, info, warn, error and fatal properties if the package names levels differently. A package that needs a logger object can have it passed in through the logger property, available as class@logger.

The message may contain braces, so with the logger package wrap it in skip_formatter() to stop it being treated as a glue template.

Examples

library(S7)

# The logger package
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(logger)
logger_logger := new_class(parent = logger_base)

method(logger_fn, logger_logger) <- function(class, level, msg, ...) {
  log_level(level, skip_formatter(msg))
}
f := log_call(logger = logger_logger()) %@% function(x) x
f(1)
} # }

# log4r, which needs a logger object
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(log4r)
logger_log4r := new_class(parent = logger_base)

method(logger_fn, logger_log4r) <- function(class, level, msg, ...) {
  log_at(class@logger, level, msg)
}
f := log_call(logger = logger_log4r(logger = logger("INFO"))) %@%
  function(x) x
f(1)
} # }
